## Submitting

Call submit_patch as soon as you have a plausible fix, even a partial one,
and call it again after every improvement. submit_patch does not count
against your tool-call budget and costs you nothing. If you run out of
context or time, the last submitted patch is what gets scored — an early
mediocre patch always beats losing your work.

## Scratch files

Write any reproduction or debugging script to /tmp, never inside /workspace.
Everything left in /workspace becomes part of your submitted patch.
Do not modify test files, conftest.py or pytest.ini — those changes are
stripped before grading, so editing them wastes tool calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

Start with grep:
  run_command("grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")
Read files only after grep has narrowed the candidates. Keep read_file
ranges tight — each call returns at most 150 lines and consumes context
you will need later.

    *,
    request: Union[Request, WebSocket],
    dependant: Dependant,

    )

import inspect
from functools import partial
import asyncio

async def async_func():
    return "async"

def sync_func():
    return "sync"

class CallableClass:
    async def __call__(self):
        return "async_class"
    
    def __call_sync__(self):
        return "sync_class"

class SyncCallableClass:
    def __call__(self):
        return "sync_class"

async def test():
    p_async = partial(async_func)
    p_sync = partial(sync_func)
    
    cc_async = CallableClass()
    p_cc_async = partial(cc_async)
    
    cc_sync = SyncCallableClass()
    p_cc_sync = partial(cc_sync)

    print(f"async_func: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(async_func)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(async_func)}")
    print(f"p_async: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(p_async)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(p_async)}")
    
    print(f"sync_func: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(sync_func)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(sync_func)}")
    print(f"p_sync: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(p_sync)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(p_sync)}")
    
    print(f"cc_async: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(cc_async)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(cc_async)}")
    print(f"p_cc_async: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(p_cc_async)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(p_cc_async)}")
    
    print(f"cc_sync: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(cc_sync)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(cc_sync)}")
    print(f"p_cc_sync: isroutine={inspect.isroutine(p_cc_sync)}, iscoroutinefunction={asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(p_cc_sync)}")

asyncio.run(test())

import inspect
from functools import partial
import asyncio

async def async_func():
    return 'async'

class CallableClass:
    async def __call__(self):
        return 'async_class'

cc = CallableClass()

def get_base_callable(callable_obj):
    call = inspect.unwrap(callable_obj)
    while hasattr(call, 'func') and callable(call.func):
        call = call.func
        call = inspect.unwrap(call)
    return call

p_async = partial(async_func)
p_cc = partial(cc)
p_p_cc = partial(p_cc)

print(f'base(p_async): {get_base_callable(p_async) == async_func}')
print(f'base(p_cc): {get_base_callable(p_cc) == cc}')
print(f'base(p_p_cc): {get_base_callable(p_p_cc) == cc}')
"
